problemSignature.symptom: Generated routed fixture initially failed KiCad load or created shorts/unconnected items after netted pads and tracks were added.

rootCause: The fixture writer emitted numeric net references in tracks/pads while known-good BoardForge KiCad files use net names, and the pad-world coordinate transform used the wrong rotation sign for KiCad footprint pad coordinates.
fixSummary: Emit named nets on pads and segments, use KiCad-compatible clockwise pad rotation math, widen placeholder pad pitch, and keep this beginner odd-shape fixture to a small clean routed net set.

testsAdded: fixture runner creates odd-shape preroute KiCad artifacts without fake manufacturing

recipe: Use KiCad-compatible net names on generated tracks and pads.
Use clockwise pad rotation when converting footprint-local pad offsets to board coordinates.
Run KiCad DRC after generated copper is written.
If a fixture is meant to prove the product pipeline, start with a small clean routed net set before increasing density.
safetyRules: Never treat generated copper as valid until KiCad loads the board and reports DRC/ERC evidence.
Do not hide command-load failures as DRC counts.
Do not use dense generated fixtures as beginner proof if a smaller routed fixture better validates the platform.
